# Drawing Icon

## Summary
A line icon that draws itself stroke by stroke, holds for a beat, then erases and starts again — used as the "working" glyph for a specific kind of activity (searching, thinking, writing, making an image). Because it's the activity's own icon rather than a generic spinner, it says *what* is happening as well as *that* something is happening.

## When to use
- Next to a status label while an agent runs a step whose kind you know ("Searching the web", "Creating image").
- In tool-call chips, step lists or traces where each step type already has an icon — animate the icon of the step that is running.
- When duration is unknown and you want a calmer, more characterful signal than a spinner.

## When not to use
- When you know real progress — use a progress bar.
- For more than one running step in the same view; several icons drawing at once reads as noise. Animate only the active one and show the rest static.
- With dense, filled or very detailed icons — the effect needs a few clean strokes to read.
- As decoration on idle UI. Motion should mean "working right now".

## Anatomy
- Icon: a 24×24 stroke icon split into its individual paths (2–7 strokes works best), drawn in path order.
- Optional ghost: a faint, static copy of the full icon underneath, so the shape is recognisable at every frame, including the empty one.
- Label (outside the component): the present-participle verb for the step.

## Behavior
- Each stroke animates its dash offset: draw on (~45% of the loop), hold fully drawn (~20%), then slide off the far end (~35%), easing in and out. Default loop is 3.6s.
- Strokes start staggered (default 0.3s apart), so the icon builds up in sequence rather than all at once.
- Works for any path: every stroke is normalised with `pathLength="1"`, so one keyframe set fits every shape.
- When the step changes, swap the icon (remount it so it starts drawing from empty) and the label together.
- When the step finishes, pause it: it settles on the fully drawn icon, which then becomes the step's static "done" glyph.

## Content guidelines
- Pick the icon that matches the actual activity; don't show a globe unless something is actually being searched.
- Pair it with a short label — the icon alone is a hint, not a status.
- Order paths so the drawing reads naturally: outline first, details last.

## Accessibility
- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`) when a visible label sits next to it; otherwise pass a `label` so it's announced as an image.
- Put the status label in an `aria-live="polite"` region so step changes are announced.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the icon is shown fully drawn and only gently pulses its opacity.

## Related patterns
- **Thinking Loader** — Use it as well, replacing its static glyph with a Drawing Icon for the step that is running.
- **Tool Call Chip** — Use it as well to animate the chip's icon while the call runs.
- **Analysis List** — Use it as well to animate only the active step's icon.

## Default implementation (Tailwind v4 + Radix + Motion)

This is the catalogue's own reference implementation — use it verbatim when the
host project has no established design system, or when the user asks for
"the demoed look." When the host project has its own design system, treat

(Anatomy, Behavior, Content guidelines, Accessibility) and re-express the
markup, styling, and motion using that system's own components/tokens
instead of copying these Tailwind classes or the Motion API.

"use client";

import * as React from "react";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

/**
 * Stroke paths for a few 24×24 line icons (Lucide, ISC). Circles are written
 * as two arcs so every shape is a `<path>` that can be "drawn".
 */
export const DRAWING_ICONS = {

    "M9 18h6",
    "M10 22h4",
  ],
  pen: [
    "M21.174 6.812a1 1 0 0 0-3.986-3.987L3.842 16.174a2 2 0 0 0-.5.83l-1.321 4.352a.5.5 0 0 0 .623.622l4.353-1.32a2 2 0 0 0 .83-.497z",
    "M13 21h8",
  ],
  telescope: [
    "m10.065 12.493-6.18 1.318a.934.934 0 0 1-1.108-.702l-.537-2.15a1.07 1.07 0 0 1 .691-1.265l13.504-4.44",
    "M16.485 5.94a2 2 0 0 1 1.455-2.425l1.09-.272a1 1 0 0 1 1.212.727l1.515 6.06a1 1 0 0 1-.727 1.213l-1.09.272a2 2 0 0 1-2.425-1.455z",
    "m13.56 11.747 4.332-.924",
    "m6.158 8.633 1.114 4.456",
    "M10 13a2 2 0 1 0 4 0a2 2 0 1 0-4 0",
    "m8 21 3.105-6.21",
    "m16 21-3.105-6.21",
  ],
} satisfies Record<string, string[]>;

export type DrawingIconName = keyof typeof DRAWING_ICONS;

export interface DrawingIconProps {
  /** A preset name, or your own list of 24×24 stroke path `d` strings, drawn in order. */
  icon: DrawingIconName | string[];
  /** Rendered size in px. */
  size?: number;
  /** Length of one draw → hold → erase loop, in seconds. */
  duration?: number;
  /** Delay between consecutive strokes starting, in seconds. */
  stagger?: number;
  /** Keep a faint copy of the full icon underneath so its shape is always readable. */
  ghost?: boolean;
  /** Pause on the fully drawn icon (e.g. when the work it stands for finishes). */
  paused?: boolean;
  /** Accessible label. Omit when a visible text label sits next to the icon. */
  label?: string;
  className?: string;
}

/*
 * Every path gets pathLength="1", so a dasharray of 1 is exactly one stroke
 * long whatever the real geometry: offset 1 hides it, 0 shows it, -1 slides
 * it off the far end. One keyframe set then draws any shape.
 */
const STYLES = `
@keyframes drawing-icon-stroke {
  0% { stroke-dashoffset: 1; }
  45%, 65% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  100% { stroke-dashoffset: -1; }
}
.drawing-icon [data-stroke] {
  stroke-dasharray: 1;
  stroke-dashoffset: 1;
  animation: drawing-icon-stroke var(--draw-duration) ease-in-out infinite;
  animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * var(--draw-stagger));
}
.drawing-icon[data-paused] [data-stroke] {
  animation: none;
  stroke-dashoffset: 0;
  transition: stroke-dashoffset 0.3s ease-out;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .drawing-icon [data-stroke] {
    animation: none;
    stroke-dashoffset: 0;
  }
  .drawing-icon:not([data-paused]) {
    animation: drawing-icon-pulse 1.6s ease-in-out infinite;
  }
}
@keyframes drawing-icon-pulse {
  50% { opacity: 0.45; }
}
`;

export function DrawingIcon({
  icon,
  size = 16,
  duration = 3.6,
  stagger = 0.3,
  ghost = false,
  paused = false,
  label,
  className,
}: DrawingIconProps) {
  const paths = typeof icon === "string" ? DRAWING_ICONS[icon] : icon;

  return (
    <svg
      xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
      width={size}
      height={size}
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth={2}
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
      role={label ? "img" : undefined}
      aria-label={label}
      aria-hidden={label ? undefined : true}
      data-paused={paused ? "" : undefined}
      className={cn("drawing-icon shrink-0", className)}
      style={
        {
          "--draw-duration": `${duration}s`,
          "--draw-stagger": `${stagger}s`,
        } as React.CSSProperties
      }
    >
      <style>{STYLES}</style>
      {ghost && (
        <g opacity={0.15}>
          {paths.map((d, i) => (
            <path key={i} d={d} />
          ))}
        </g>
      )}
      {paths.map((d, i) => (
        <path
          key={i}
          d={d}
          pathLength={1}
          data-stroke=""
          style={{ "--i": i } as React.CSSProperties}
        />
      ))}
    </svg>
  );
}
